successors.name: British Cape Colony
successors.text: the Cape taken by the British in January 1806 after the Battle of Blaauwberg

capitals.name: Cape Town (Kaapstad), Castle of Good Hope

ledger.x: 1652: the Dutch East India Company founds the Cape of Good Hope Waystation at Cape Town.
1660: the Khoekhoe cede the land round the settlement.
1672: Commissioner Arnout van Overbeke buys the Cape territory.
April 1721: the Dutch govern Delagoa Bay from the Cape.
December 1730: the Dutch abandon Delagoa Bay.
1734: the Cape grows to the Western Cape west of about 22 E.
1745: a magistracy is set up at Swellendam.
1769: the colony grows to 156,768 km2 in Cliopatria's shape (Western Cape and the south of the Northern Cape).
November 1780: the Great Fish River becomes the eastern boundary.
1795: the Graaff-Reinet district proclaims a republic.
7 August 1795: the British occupy the Cape.
1 March 1803: the Cape returns to Dutch rule.
1803: the Cape becomes a colony of the Batavian Republic.
January 1806: the British retake the Cape.

wars.name: First Frontier War (First Xhosa War)
wars.outcome: Van Plettenberg declared the Great Fish River the eastern border in November 1780; Van Jaarsveld disbanded his commandos on 19 July 1781.

wars.name: British invasion of the Cape (Battle of Muizenberg)
wars.outcome: The British occupied the Cape from 7 August 1795 (infobox); the Dutch militia lost at Muizenberg.

wars.name: Battle of Blaauwberg (second British occupation)
wars.outcome: British victory; the Cape was occupied 8-18 January 1806 and ceded formally in 1814.

certainty.note: No frontier is given before 1745; the settled districts shade into Khoekhoe and trekboer country.
The Great Fish River line (declared November 1780) is a river line but the settlers and the Xhosa crossed it; the northern edge in the Karoo is approximate.
